findings.title: forceOpen on Accordion has no test
findings.problem: The new forceOpen prop opens the accordion via useEffect and is used at AssistantForm (forceOpen={!!errors.headroom_config}). No test sets forceOpen; the integration test for a server strategy error clicks the Context accordion open itself before saving, so it cannot observe the behavior.
findings.impact: If the effect is removed or not wired, the server strategy error stays hidden inside a collapsed accordion and the user sees only a toast, with every test still passing.
findings.recommendation: In Accordion.test.tsx render with defaultOpen={false} forceOpen={false}, assert content hidden, rerender with forceOpen={true}, assert visible. In HeadroomSection.integration.test do not click the Context accordion before Save in the server-error case.
findings.check_notes: Accordion.test.tsx now rerenders defaultOpen=false forceOpen false->true and asserts aria-expanded and grid-rows change; Accordion.tsx effect at line 48 confirmed; integration test no longer opens Context accordion before Save.

findings.title: Headroom analytics gate and wiring untested

InsightsTab.test.tsx mocks useFeatureFlag with one return value for every flag and asserts only the routing section; no test covers HeadroomAnalyticsSection or its widget props.
findings.impact: Gating on the wrong flag, or removing the gate, would make requests to a 404-ing endpoint with the flag off and go unnoticed; the endpoint and metric wiring is unverified.
findings.recommendation: In InsightsTab.test.tsx mock useFeatureFlag per flag name, mock HeadroomAnalyticsSection with a testid, assert absent when only the routing flag is on and present when only the headroom flag is on. Add a HeadroomAnalyticsSection test asserting HEADROOM_SUMMARY, the timeseries labelField/series and HEADROOM_BY_STRATEGY table wiring.
findings.check_notes: InsightsTab.test.tsx mocks useFeatureFlag per flag name and asserts the Headroom section shown only for FEATURE_FLAGS.HEADROOM; new HeadroomAnalyticsSection.test.tsx asserts summary, timeseries and strategy-table wiring. InsightsTab.tsx gate at line 153 confirmed.

findings.title: Node-level headroom save path in AssistantTab untested
findings.problem: AssistantTab writes headroom into the assistant actor config via buildHeadroom on save and compares it with initialHeadroomRef for isDirty. AssistantTab.test.tsx has no headroom coverage, and HeadroomPanel/AdvancedConfigTab tests never exercise this path.

Add a flag-off case asserting an existing YAML headroom block is preserved, and an inherited={config.headroom} case.

findings.title: Headroom panel crashes on null headroom block
findings.problem: hasOverride is computed as value !== undefined && Object.keys(value).length > 0. A workflow YAML with a bare `headroom:` key parses to null, YamlPanel.validateYaml performs no headroom shape check, and the headroom completer itself inserts a bare `headroom:`. The null reaches HeadroomPanel through config.headroom in AdvancedConfigTab and AssistantTab, and Object.keys(null) throws.
findings.impact: Opening the workflow or node config panel with the flag on throws during render after a user saves YAML containing a bare headroom key; the panel (potentially the editor) crashes.
findings.recommendation: const hasOverride = !!value && Object.keys(value).length > 0, and consider coercing a non-object config.headroom to undefined where AdvancedConfigTab and AssistantTab read it.
findings.check_notes: HeadroomPanel.tsx hasOverride now uses !!value && Object.keys(value).length > 0; regression test renders with null value without throwing.
